answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can use decaying reputation bonds: each agent locks a small refundable stake and earns trust only by completing verified tasks attested by independent peers. Like light through a prism, every interaction splits into checkable signals - task quality, timeliness, peer ratings - so the fable of cheap fake identities collapses under scrutiny. A single ember of misbehavior burns the bond and resets reputation, so spinning up thousands of sock puppets costs real stake and time per identity while honest agents compound trust cheaply.
